bloques.html_en: What is acid rain? Acid rain is rain (or snow, fog or mist) that has become acidic because polluting gases have mixed with the water in the clouds. It looks like normal rain — but it damages plants, animals, water and even buildings.

🔥 What causes it?

  • Burning fossil fuels — coal, oil and gas — in factories and power stations.
  • Cars, buses and lorries burning petrol and diesel.
  • A small amount comes from nature too, like volcanoes.

⭐ Learn these two gases by heart:
Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and Nitrogen oxides (NOₓ).
They mix with water in the air and turn into sulfuric acid and nitric acid.
💧 How is acid rain formed? (5 steps)
💨 The wind can carry those gases very far. Acid rain can fall in a country hundreds of kilometres away from the factory that made the pollution!
🌍 Effects on the environment

🔗 Acid rain breaks the food chain!
In a freshwater lake: shrimps → fish → herons.
If the acid kills the shrimps, the fish have no food and die. Then the herons have no fish to eat, so they die or fly away. One dead animal affects everything above it in the food chain.

✅ Ways to reduce acid rain

  • 🔆 Use renewable energy — solar panels, wind turbines, water power — instead of burning coal.
  • 💡 Use less electricity: turn off lights, TVs and chargers you are not using.
  • 🚲 Walk, cycle, share a car or take the bus instead of one car per person.
  • 🏭 Put filters (scrubbers) on factory chimneys to trap the gases before they escape.
  • 🚗 Use catalytic converters and cleaner fuels in cars.
  • 🌱 Plant trees and add lime to damaged lakes to help them recover.
Exam sentence you can use: "Acid rain is formed when sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning fossil fuels mix with water in the atmosphere and fall as acidic rain."

What is recycling? Recycling means taking used materials and turning them into new things instead of throwing them away as rubbish. An old plastic bottle can become a new bottle — or even a fleece jacket!

❓ Why is recycling important?

  • 🌳 It saves natural resources — trees, oil, sand and metal stay in the ground.
  • ⚡ It saves energy. Making a can from recycled aluminium uses far less energy than making a brand-new one.
  • 🗑️ It means less rubbish in landfills, so we need fewer of them.
  • 💨 It creates less pollution in the air, soil and water.
  • 🐢 It protects animals and their habitats.

📦 Recyclable materials
Golden rule: rinse it first! Dirty containers with food on them can spoil a whole batch of recycling. 🚿
🔺 The 3 Rs — in this exact order
Don't mix these up! 🔁 Reuse = the same object is used again (refilling a bottle). ♻️ Recycle = the object is broken down and made into a new object (a bottle becomes a T-shirt).

🗑️ What happens if we throw away too much trash?

  • Landfills fill up and take over land where plants and animals used to live.
  • Rubbish gives off harmful gases and poisons that leak into the soil and water.
  • Plastic ends up in rivers and the sea. 🐋 Animals eat it or get trapped in it and die.
  • Plastic takes hundreds of years to break down.
Exam sentence you can use: "Recycling is important because it saves natural resources and energy, reduces the amount of rubbish in landfills, and protects animals and the environment from pollution."

⚡ A CONDUCTOR is a material that lets electric current pass through it easily.
🚫 An INSULATOR is a material that does NOT let electric current pass through it.
Easy way to remember: if it is a metal, it is almost always a conductor. If it is not a metal (plastic, rubber, glass, wood), it is almost always an insulator. 🧲
📋 Examples of each
🛠️ Uses — why we need BOTH
⚠️ Safety! Your body and water are conductors too. Never touch plugs or switches with wet hands, and never poke anything metal into a socket.
Exam sentence you can use: "Electrical wires are covered with plastic because plastic is an insulator. It stops the electricity from escaping and keeps people safe from electric shocks."
📖 The 10 words you MUST know
The #1 mistake: a cell is ONE. A battery is TWO OR MORE cells joined together. The thing in your TV remote is really a cell, even though everyone calls it a battery! 😄
🔄 Parts of a simple circuit
⚙️ How does an electric circuit work?

The cell pushes electric charge out. The charge travels along the wires, goes through the bulb (making it light up), and comes all the way back to the cell. It must go round in a complete loop — like a running track. 🏃‍♂️
✅ Complete vs ❌ Incomplete (open) circuits
Why does a bulb not light in an open circuit? Because the path is broken, so the electric current cannot flow through the bulb. Learn that sentence! ✏️

Circuit symbols are simple drawings that represent electrical components. They help us draw circuits clearly and quickly — everyone in the world uses the same ones, so any scientist can read your diagram. 🌍
⚡ The 7 symbols you need

Cell vs Battery symbol: count the pairs of lines!
1 pair = cell. 2 or more pairs = battery.
Bulb vs Motor: both are circles. X inside = bulb (light 💡). M inside = motor (movement ⚙️).
📐 Reading a circuit diagram

Follow the wire with your finger, starting at the cell. Say the name of every symbol you pass. When you get back to the cell — that's the whole circuit! If your finger has to jump a gap, the circuit is open and nothing will work.
Rules for drawing: ✏️ use a ruler for every wire · draw symbols only, never the real objects · make corners into right angles · label each component.
